recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit for FHIR-36693. Any remaining review of the broader Device.property, DeviceMetric, and Observation boundary should be handled under FHIR-39322 or a successor rather than by reapplying the exact 2022 FHIR-36693 wording.
issue_request: FHIR-36693 was a Published/Persuasive R5 OO change request to update Device.property so it distinguished device-instance properties from DeviceDefinition capabilities, and to update Device.specialization so it described standards the device adheres to and may be certified to for communication, performance, process, or measurement capabilities.
initial_application: The issue was applied by f357d3bbda13eb7ad310dccfc812715b3d1afe02, merged by d8612d0db8b4bdbfb09bae8f0a71bc8e660a705c, which changed Device.specialization and Device.property definitions in source/device/structuredefinition-Device.xml. The Device resource is active in source/fhir.ini, so that source file is in current build scope.
additional_context: FHIR-36154 reintroduced Device.specialization shortly before this clarification. Later Published issues FHIR-39084 and FHIR-39242 renamed Device.specialization to Device.conformsTo and broadened the wording to standards, specifications, formal guidance, certification, regulation, and related conformance models; those issues are already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-39322, not decided here because it remains Resolved - change required, explains the later static-property wording now present in source.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current Device.conformsTo preserves the specialization standards/certification meaning under the later Published element name, and current Device.property plus its comment preserves the intended distinction from DeviceDefinition while incorporating the later static-property clarification.
